 Jerusalem Post / Health & Wellness / Health and Wellness Around the World Post-summer pigmentation? These are the mistakes you are making
 Even using sunscreen does not guarantee full protection against pigmentation spots. Yafa Maximov explains what may lie behind the phenomenon and which mistakes to avoid.
 Follow us on Google A woman with pigmentation applying cream. ( photo credit : SHUTTERSTOCK ) By WALLA! HEALTH OCTOBER 25, 2026 08:00 You returned from vacation, your tan is starting to fade, and suddenly dark spots appear on your forehead, cheeks, or above your upper lip. The phenomenon may seem surprising, especially if you were careful to wear a hat, stay in the shade, and apply sunscreen. However, pigmentation changes are not always noticeable immediately after sun exposure, and sometimes they become more prominent only later on.
 Why does this happen, what is the link between sun exposure and the appearance of spots, and how should skin be treated without worsening the situation? Yafa Maximov, owner of a beauty-tech clinic chain and former chairwoman of the Cosmeticians Association, explains what is important to know about post-vacation pigmentation.
 Why do spots not always appear immediately? 
 Not all sun damage manifests in redness or an immediate burn. In response to radiation exposure, the melanocyte cells in the skin produce melanin, the pigment responsible for skin color. Changes in tone may develop gradually, which is why spots do not always appear at full intensity immediately following exposure.
 Sometimes, as the tan begins to fade, areas where more pigment has accumulated become visible to the eye. The process is influenced by skin type, the extent of sun exposure, hormonal factors , and an individual tendency toward pigmentation. Among other things, sun exposure can worsen melasma – a condition that manifests in brown spots, mainly on the face.
 It is important to remember that not every new spot is necessarily pigmentation caused by the vacation. If a new spot appears, if it changes, or if there is any doubt regarding its nature, it is advisable to consult a dermatologist for a diagnosis.
 Sunscreen is a central part of skin protection, but even using a product with a high protection factor does not guarantee complete prevention of pigmentation. (credit: SHUTTERSTOCK) Applied SPF 50 sunscreen and spots appeared anyway? 
 Sunscreen is a central part of skin protection , but even using a product with a high protection factor does not guarantee complete prevention of pigmentation. The degree of protection depends, among other things, on the amount of product applied, the frequency of reapplication, and cumulative sun exposure.
 In cases of melasma, UVA radiation and visible light may also contribute to worsening the spots. Therefore, it is advisable to choose a broad-spectrum sunscreen, be diligent about applying an adequate amount, and reapply it according to instructions, especially after swimming, sweating, or towel drying. A wide-brimmed hat, staying in the shade, and reducing exposure during hours when radiation is strong complete the protection.
 Maximov notes that many women are surprised to discover spots even after being diligent with sunscreen. According to her, it is important to treat sun protection as part of a permanent skincare routine and not just as an action taken during a vacation.
 Three mistakes to avoid when spots appear 
 1. Aggressive use of peels and acids 
When seeing a dark spot, the temptation to try removing it quickly can be great. But hard scrubbing or using active products in high concentrations can cause irritation and inflammation. In some people, especially those with skin prone to it, inflammation can lead to post-inflammatory pigmentation – meaning the appearance of spots as a result of the irritation itself.
 Therefore, it is better to avoid aggressive scrubbing and trying to forcibly peel the spot. If the skin is red, sensitive, or irritated after the vacation, it is advisable to let it calm down before resuming the use of active products.
 2. Returning to retinol and active ingredients too quickly 
Retinol and other active ingredients may be integrated into the treatment of certain skin problems, but they can also cause dryness, redness, and irritation, especially when the skin is sensitive. After prolonged exposure to the sun , or swimming in the sea or pool, it is advisable to examine the condition of the skin and not rush back to an intensive routine.
 If the skin is not irritated, a gradual return to previously used products can be considered, according to product instructions and professional guidance. In case of significant burning or redness, it is recommended to stop use and seek advice.
 3. Focusing on brightening without restoring the skin barrier 
Pigmentation treatment does not end with trying to brighten the spots. A basic skincare routine that includes gentle cleansing, moisturizer, and daily sun protection helps maintain the skin barrier and reduces the risk of further irritation.
 There is no need to overload several active products at the same time. An uncoordinated combination of products can increase sensitivity, so it is better to choose a simple routine and add ingredients gradually.
 How do you treat post-vacation pigmentation? 
 The appropriate treatment depends on the type of pigmentation, its depth, skin tone, and the factors that led to its appearance. There is no single method suitable for all spots, and not every cosmetic treatment is suitable for every skin type.
 First stage: Soothing and protection. If the skin is irritated, it is recommended to focus on gentle cleansing, hydration, and strict sun protection. Products with ingredients like ceramides or niacinamide can be considered, depending on skin tolerance. There is no need to immediately start intensive brightening treatment.
 Second stage: Choosing products for pigmentation treatment. Ingredients such as azelaic acid and other brightening components may help in certain cases, but their suitability depends on diagnosis and skin condition. Before combining acids or active ingredients in high concentrations, it is advisable to receive professional guidance, especially if the spots are new or if the skin is prone to sensitivity.
 Third stage: Considering professional treatments. In certain cases, in-clinic treatments can be considered, including medical peels or light-based devices. However, such treatments are not suitable for all types of pigmentation, and may actually worsen spots in some patients, especially if they cause inflammation. Therefore, it is important to undergo a diagnosis by a dermatologist or an appropriate medical professional before choosing a treatment, and not rely solely on the type of device.
 According to Maximov, pigmentation treatment requires patience and personalization, and a significant change cannot always be achieved in a single treatment. The duration of treatment and its results vary depending on the type of spots, their depth, and the individual response of the skin.
 Ultimately, the appearance of spots after vacation is not necessarily a sign that all strict adherence to sun protection was in vain. It is indeed a reminder that radiation protection must be consistent, and that when new pigmentation appears, it is better not to rush to treat it through aggressive means. Proper diagnosis, a tailored skincare routine, and daily sun protection are a good starting point for dealing with the phenomenon.
